summary: The note describes the design of the first ₹10 coin, minted in 2005 in India. It details the obverse, which has the lettering 'भारत' and 'INDIA', the Lion capital with 'Satyameva Jayate' in Hindi, and the mint date, and the reverse, which shows a cross with a dot in each quadrant and the denomination lettering. The source is a brief, Wikipedia-derived excerpt with no further history or context.
one_line: Design description of the first 2005 Indian ₹10 coin, covering its 27 mm obverse and reverse inscriptions and motifs.
key_facts: The first ₹10 coin was minted in 2005.
The first ₹10 coin had a diameter of 27 mm.
The obverse of the first ₹10 coin bears the lettering 'भारत' and 'INDIA' on the top.
The obverse of the first ₹10 coin features the Lion capital with 'Satyameva Jayate' in Hindi below at left.
The obverse of the first ₹10 coin shows the date of mint below the Lion capital.
The reverse of the first ₹10 coin features four heads sharing a common body.
The reverse of the first ₹10 coin shows a cross with a dot in each quadrant in the center.
The reverse of the first ₹10 coin has the lettering 'दस रुपये' on the outer ring.
The reverse of the first ₹10 coin has the lettering 'TEN RUPEES' on the outer ring.
